target.title: feat(ios): pair multiple gateways and switch between them without re-pairing
target.body:
Related: #100700

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app can hold exactly one paired gateway. Anyone running more than one gateway (home machine plus a server, personal plus work) has to re-enter the endpoint and credentials every time they want to talk to a different one, and pairing a second gateway silently destroys the first gateway's stored credentials because the credential bundle is a single Keychain slot per install.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds first-class multi-gateway support, app-side only (no protocol changes):

- **Paired-gateway registry**: a single Keychain entry (`gateway-registry`) records every paired gateway plus the active selection, keyed by the same per-gateway `stableID` that already scopes TLS pins, chat-cache databases, and per-gateway preferences. It replaces the old single `lastConnection` record; a one-time migration folds the legacy Keychain entry and the older `gateway.last.*` UserDefaults into the registry, then deletes them. Runtime reads only the registry.
- **Per-gateway credential bundles**: the credential bundle account is now scoped per gateway (`gateway-credentials.<instanceId>.<stableID>`), with a one-time migration of the legacy unscoped bundle to its owner. Saving credentials for one gateway no longer erases another gateway's bundle.
- **Switching and forgetting** (`GatewayConnectionController.switchToGateway` / `forgetGateway`): switching reuses the existing force-reconnect teardown/rebuild; discovered gateways that are not currently visible fail with a clear message. Forget removes the registry entry, scoped credentials, TLS pin, per-gateway defaults, device-auth tokens (app and share-extension identities), share-relay config when owned by that gateway, and the per-gateway chat-cache database, handling forget-during-connect races.
- **Push follows the active gateway**: the APNs registration dedupe was global (`apnsLastRegisteredTokenHex`), so after a switch the new gateway never received `push.apns.register` on direct transport; the dedupe is now (token, gateway) scoped.
- **UI**: a Paired Gateways list in the gateway settings (active marker, tap to switch, swipe/context-menu forget with confirmation) and a quick-switch menu on the gateway row when more than one gateway is paired, using branded typography throughout.

## User Impact

Users can pair the app with any number of gateways and switch between them from Settings without pairing again. Credentials, TLS trust, cached chats, and per-gateway preferences stay strictly per gateway; push registration and exec-approval notifications follow the active gateway; forgetting a gateway removes all of its stored state.

## Evidence

- Focused suites green on the iOS simulator after rebasing onto current main: `GatewaySettingsStoreTests`, `GatewayConnectionControllerTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests` — 88 tests, 0 failures (`xcodebuild test -only-testing:...`).
- New coverage: registry CRUD and deterministic persistence; migrations (manual/discovered last-connection, legacy defaults, legacy unscoped credential bundle) with idempotence; credential isolation across gateways (save B leaves A intact; forget B leaves A); switch-to-manual applies the right stableID/URL; switch-to-undiscoverable fails without touching state; forget races (pending trust handoff, live replacement route, repeated device-auth cleanup after teardown); per-gateway chat-cache isolation across an active-gateway switch; gateway-scoped push registration dedupe.
- SwiftFormat lint lane clean; full app build green.
- Structured review (Codex, gpt-5.5) over the full bundle: no actionable findings.
- Docs updated: `docs/platforms/ios.md` (multiple gateways section); iOS app changelog entry added.
